info.name: CourtMesh API: Indian Court Cases
info.description:
# CourtMesh API: Indian court cases

A REST API over Indian court judgments and orders: the Supreme Court, every High Court, District Courts and tribunals. Search by keyword or by meaning, pull a single judgment with its parties and bench, read a structured AI analysis, follow a matter's order sheet over time, and download the source PDF.

Base URL: `https://research.courtmesh.ai/api/v1/prod`

## Getting a key

API keys are issued from the CourtMesh dashboard at https://research.courtmesh.ai. A key looks like `cm-XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX-XXXX`. Keys issued before the rename start with `vv-` and still work.

## Authentication

Every endpoint except `GET /health` needs a key. Two header forms are accepted:

```
Authorization: Bearer cm-your-key-here
```

```
X-API-Key: cm-your-key-here
```

This collection uses the bearer form at the collection level, so set the `apiKey` variable once and every request inherits it.

## Collection variables

| variable | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| baseUrl | API root. Defaults to the production host |
| apiKey | Your API key. Leave it out of source control, use a Postman environment |
| caseId | A case identifier used by the case level requests. Accepts a 24 character hexadecimal case id or a case number |
| requestId | A timeline job id returned by POST /request-timeline |
| profileRequestId | A full mode party profile id (ppr_...) returned by POST /party/profile |
| userId | A user id for GET /audit's userId query param. Call GET /me first to get your own id |
| cnr | A CNR such as ZZAB010000012024, used by the CNR lookup and monitoring requests |
| watchlistId | A watchlist id (wl_...) from Create a watchlist |
| webhookId | A webhook id (wh_...) from Create a webhook |
| deliveryId | A delivery id (whd_...) from List webhook deliveries |
| changesCursor | The pagination.nextCursor from the previous List changes call |
| documentId | A document id from List the orders of a case |
| matterId | A 24 character matter id, used by the cause listings of one matter |
| courtKey | A court key from a cause listing, used by the court cause list |
| actSlug | An act slug such as indian-penal-code-1860, used by the Acts and Sections requests |
| sectionSlug | A provision slug such as section-302, used by the Acts and Sections requests |

## Response envelope

Every endpoint except `GET /health` returns:

```json
{ "success": true, "data": {}, "meta": {}, "pagination": {} }
```

`meta` and `pagination` appear only where the endpoint provides them. Failures return `{ "success": false, "error": "..." }`, with an extra `details` array of human readable messages when request validation failed.

Authentication and rate limit failures come from middleware and are not wrapped, they are a bare `{ "error": "..." }`.

Every response, success or failure, carries an `X-Request-Id` response header. Some endpoints (for example `GET /usage`, `POST /party/screen/batch`) also echo it as `meta.requestId` in the body; quote either one when reporting a problem to CourtMesh support.

## Rate limits

10 requests per minute per API key. Successful responses carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`. A 429 body carries `retryAfter` in seconds and `resetTime` as an ISO timestamp. Back off and retry, do not hammer.

## Pagination

Two shapes, because the two search endpoints page differently.

`POST /search/cases` returns `{ total, hasMore, page, limit, nextCursor }`. There is no `totalPages`. For deep pagination, send the previous `nextCursor` back as `searchAfter`, in which case `page` is omitted from the response.

`POST /search/cases/semantic` returns `{ page, limit, total, totalPages, hasMore }`, where `total` and `totalPages` are estimates that only become exact on the final page.

## Idempotency

POST /party/screen, POST /party/screen/batch, POST /party/profile, POST /cases/{id}/analyze, POST /cases/{id}/analyze-consolidated and POST /request-timeline each accept an optional `Idempotency-Key` header, 1 to 128 characters, `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`. Of the monitoring requests, only create watchlist and add cases to a watchlist honour it (the webhook requests do not take one). The cause list check (POST /cause-lists/check) honours it too. Every request for these endpoints in this collection carries one, defaulted to Postman's `{{$guid}}` dynamic variable (a fresh UUID v4 generated on every send).

The key is scoped per API key for 24 hours: replaying the same key with the same request body returns the original 2xx response again, with response header `Idempotency-Replayed: true`, and no new charge. The same key with a different body is refused with 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. A request with this key still being processed is refused with 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`. A malformed key is refused with 400 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID`.

Because `{{$guid}}` regenerates on every send, re-sending one of these requests from the Postman UI runs as a new, separately charged call each time, by design. To deliberately exercise the replay behaviour, replace the header value with a fixed string before sending the same request twice.

item.description: Keyword search and semantic search over Indian court judgments.

request.description:
Keyword search across Indian court judgments.

`query` is required and must be at least one character after trimming. Everything else is optional.

Body fields:

| field | type | rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| query | string | required, trimmed, minimum length 1 |
| court | string or string array | optional |
| year | integer, a four digit string, or an array of either | optional. Integers must be between 1947 and the current year |
| caseType | string or string array | optional. Values are expanded to court case type codes server side |
| caseNumber | string, or a one element string array | optional. Filters results on that single case number; a second array element is rejected with 400 ("Only one caseNumber can be filtered per request."), never silently dropped |
| judgeName | string or string array | optional |
| judges | string or string array | optional alias for judgeName |
| judge | string or string array | optional alias for judgeName |
| fromDate | string | optional, format YYYY-MM-DD |
| toDate | string | optional, format YYYY-MM-DD |
| page | integer | optional, minimum 1, default 1 |
| limit | integer | optional, 1 to 100, default 20. Each plan tier caps this lower (Free tier: 20); above the cap is rejected with 400 `PAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, and `page * limit` beyond the tier's pagination depth cap is rejected with 400 `PAGINATION_DEPTH_EXCEEDED` |
| cursor | string | optional opaque signed pagination cursor, the current mechanism. Send the previous response's `pagination.nextCursor` back unmodified to fetch the next page; a cursor issued for a different query/filters, or a malformed one, is rejected with 400 `CURSOR_INVALID` |
| searchAfter | string | optional legacy cursor. Prefer `cursor` above for new integrations |
| sortBy | "relevance", "recent" or "oldest" | optional, default "relevance". "date" is accepted too, as a deprecated alias that is applied as "recent" |

Judge precedence in the handler is judgeName, then judges, then judge.

Response `data` is an array of raw search hits. Each hit carries the stored document fields. Analysis fields such as `detailedSummary` and `holding` never appear here. Fetch a single case with GET /cases/{id} for the curated view.

Pagination on this endpoint is `{ total, hasMore, page, limit, nextCursor }`. There is no `totalPages`. `page` is omitted when you paginate with `cursor` or the legacy `searchAfter`.

`caseNumber` and `sortBy` are both real, honoured filters today: `caseNumber` narrows results to that single case number, and `relevance`, `recent` and `oldest` are all real sort orders (`date` silently maps to `recent`, and the response's `meta` carries a notice explaining the substitution). Supreme Court hits carry `sameMatter`: the other orders and documents of the same matter, newest first, each `{ caseId, decisionDate, caseType }`. Each matter appears once per page, so a page can hold fewer rows than `limit`; page with `nextCursor`, not the row count.

  "query": "trade licence cancelled without notice",
  "court": "Bombay High Court",
  "year": 2021,
  "caseType": "WP",
  "judgeName": "Deshpande",
  "fromDate": "2020-01-01",
  "toDate": "2021-12-31",
  "page": 1,
  "limit": 20,
  "sortBy": "relevance"
}

request.description:
AI search by meaning, with a language model pre step that pulls filters out of your natural language query.

`query` is required and must be at least three characters. This endpoint is billed as an AI interaction and is not available on the Free tier, which returns 403 `SEMANTIC_NOT_ALLOWED`.

Body fields:

| field | type | rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| query | string | required, trimmed, minimum length 3 |
| court | string or string array | optional |
| year | integer, a four digit string, or an array of either | optional |
| caseType | string or string array | optional |
| caseNumber | string, or a string array | optional. Digits only (for example "1234"): AI search filters case numbers numerically and cannot match a formatted string like "WP(C) 123/2024" |
| judgeName | string, or a one element string array | optional. Only one judge name is honoured per request; a second value is rejected |
| judges | same rules as judgeName | optional alias |
| judge | same rules as judgeName | optional alias |
| fromDate | string | optional, format YYYY-MM-DD |
| toDate | string | optional, format YYYY-MM-DD |
| page | integer | optional, minimum 1, default 1 |
| limit | integer | optional, 1 to 100, default 20 |
| filters | object | optional. Addresses the AI search's own filter keys directly |

request.description:
Look a case up by its CNR (Case Number Record). Any common spelling is accepted and normalised: the path value is trimmed, uppercased, and spaces, hyphens, slashes, dots and a leading `CNR`, `CNR:` or `CNR NO` are removed. A valid CNR is 16 characters, for example `ZZAB010000012024`; anything else is 400 `INVALID_CNR`.

Costs 1 credit, charged only when a record is returned (`not_found` and `pending` cost 0).

`data.status` is `found` (200, `data.case` is the same record `GET /cases/{id}` returns, including `caseStatus`, `caseStage`, `nextHearingDate`, `lastListedOn` and `orderCount`), `pending` (202, a live fetch is running: poll this same URL; `requestId` is opaque and is not accepted by `GET /get-timeline`), or `not_found` (404 with code `CASE_NOT_FOUND`; the error body also carries `cnr` and `status`). A Supreme Court CNR that is not in the corpus cannot be fetched live and is `404` at once.

Set `fetch=true` to start a live court fetch for a CNR that is not in the corpus: the call that starts the fetch returns `202 pending` and is free; the poll that returns the record is the one 1 credit charge, and a fetch the court portal cannot satisfy is free. Fetches share the daily live fetch cap with `POST /request-timeline` `refresh: true`.

If the court portal had nothing for the CNR in the last 24 hours, `fetch=true` does not ask it again: the call answers `404 CASE_NOT_FOUND` straight away. A case taken down at a party's request is reported as not found.

request.description:
Checks whether 1 to 100 CNRs that your account watches appear on a cause list that CourtMesh already holds. Body: `{ cnrs (1..100), from?, to? }`. Send both dates or neither (default: today and tomorrow, Indian calendar); at most 7 days apart. CNRs are normalised and de-duplicated in order; an invalid CNR is a 400 naming it. The call never contacts a court.

Each result has `status`:

- `listed`: a row of this case was found. `listings` holds the rows. 1 credit.
- `no_entry_found`: a list was read and no row was recognised. This is not proof that the case is not listed; `dates[].complete` says how much of each list was read. 1 credit.
- `list_not_read`: no list was held for the dates. For a District Court it can also mean the list of the case's own courtroom could not be confirmed (`dates[].status` is then `none`). Free.
- `cannot_check`: `reason` says why: `pending`, `record_unavailable`, `court_not_supported`, or a court identification reason (`no_case_identity`, `no_court_key`, `no_court_number`, `invalid_court_key`, `unsupported_court`). `courtKey` can be null. Free.
- `not_watched`: your account does not watch this CNR. Free.

`listings[].matchedBy` is `cnr`, `diary`, `key` or `related_key`; `listings[].courtKey` and `caseText` can be null (`caseText` is null on a `related_key` match or a restricted row). A 503 with `code` `SETTLEMENT_UNCONFIRMED` means the answer was ready but the charge outcome is unknown and no results were returned: do not retry yet, check your balance (`GET /usage`) first. request.description:

The `id` path parameter accepts either a 24 character hexadecimal case id or a case number. The case id is tried first, then the case number.

request.description:
Run a single AI analysis across the whole matter rather than one document.

The `id` path parameter accepts either a 24 character hexadecimal case id or a case number. The case id is tried first, then the case number.

Body: `{ "force": false }`. `force` is optional and defaults to false.

- Supreme Court matters: up to 20 documents that share the same case number.

The combined text is capped at 100,000 characters. The result is stored, so a second call without `force` returns the stored copy with `status: "already_analyzed"`.

`data.consolidatedAnalysis` carries the same keys as the single case analysis plus `benchComposition`, `opinionType`, `factPattern`, `linkedCases` and `outcome`.

Error cases: 400 when the case has no case number or no usable text, 403 when the account's AI allowance is exhausted, 404 when the case or its related documents cannot be found.

**Credits.** This call costs significantly more than POST /cases/{id}/analyze (400 credits), charged once the analysis completes; a cached `already_analyzed` response is not charged again. request.description:

Body: `{ "case_id": "<24 character hexadecimal case id>", "refresh": false }`. `case_id` is required and must be a 24 character hexadecimal case id, a case number will not work here. `refresh` is optional and defaults to false.

The response tells you what happened:
- `status: "pending"` with a `requestId`. A background job was queued. Poll GET /get-timeline/{requestId}.
- `status: "completed"` with `cached: true`, `orders` and `orderCount`. Orders were already fetched today, so you get them straight back.
- `status: "completed"` with `orderCount: 0` and an explanatory `message` for Supreme Court cases, which do not have separate orders. The case document is itself the judgment.
- `status: "failed"` with a `message`, for example when a District Court case has no CNR.

Order objects carry `id`, `title`, `caseNumber`, `decisionDate`, `court`, `caseType`, `disposalNature`, `judges`, `judge`, `petitioners`, `respondents` and `hasDocument`.

request.description:
Screen one person or company name against the case corpus for litigation history: KYC, background verification (BGV), due diligence, counterparty and compliance checks.

Body fields:

| field | type | rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| name | string | required, 2 to 200 characters |
| aliases | string array | optional, at most 7 - name plus aliases must fit the 8 name screening limit |
| entityType | "person" or "company" | required |
| purpose | "kyc", "bgv", "due_diligence", "litigation", "research" or "compliance" | required, see the DPDP note below |
| identifiers | object `{ pan, gstin, cin, llpin }` | optional, all sub fields optional strings, each format checked |
| address | object `{ city, state, stateCode }` | optional |
| knownPersons | string array | optional, at most 10, directors/partners/associates used to disambiguate |
| court | string, or a one element string array | optional, restrict to one court; a second court in the array is rejected with 400 ("one court per request for now") |
| since | string | optional, YYYY-MM-DD. Best effort post filter; using it at all forces `verdict` to `inconclusive`, see below |
| limit | integer | optional, 1 to 100, default 40 |
| adjudicate | boolean | optional, default false, see credits and the Free tier note below |
| displayThreshold | number | optional, 0 to 1, default 0.6, confidence cutoff for inclusion in `matches` |

**purpose is required under DPDP.** It is recorded as the lawful basis for processing this name and is not decorative: pick the value that genuinely describes why the screen is being run.

**A match is a case record bearing the name, not a verified identity.** Common names, aliases and identical company names across unrelated parties all produce matches. Read `confidence.band`, `evidence.matchedFields` and `evidence.disambiguatorPresent` on every match before treating it as identity confirmed, and prefer matches corroborated by an identifier (PAN, GSTIN, CIN, LLPIN) or address over name only matches. `confidence` is `{ band, score, calibrated, engine }`: `band` is one of `confirmed`, `probable`, `possible` or `unlikely`; `score` and `calibrated` are the same number (`score` is kept as a stable top level alias); `engine` is `"rules"` or `"llm"` depending on whether adjudication actually ran for that candidate. `evidence.signals` is an array of `{ name, status, weight, evidence }` objects, one per matching signal considered (for example a GSTIN match or a name similarity score), not plain strings.

**Verdict semantics.** `data.summary.verdict` is one of `matches_found`, `no_matches_found` or `inconclusive`, and the rules are stricter than they look:
- `no_matches_found` is only ever returned when `data.coverage.exhaustive` is true (every available search strategy actually ran to completion) AND nothing was withheld.
- Sending `since` always forces `inconclusive`, even when matches were found: it is a best effort post filter that cannot certify completeness in either direction.
- A withheld record (a restricted case, an id the restricted-check could not verify, a masked title) with nothing else surviving also forces `inconclusive` rather than a clean negative.
- `data.summary.matchCount` (the length of the displayed `matches` array) can read 0 while `verdict` still reads `matches_found`, when every internally matching candidate was filtered out of the display by `displayThreshold`; `verdict` describes what was found, `matchCount`/`matches` describe what is shown.

Always surface the top level `notice` field (there is no `coverage.note`) and `coverage.someRecordsWithheld` to the caller rather than silently treating an inconclusive or partial screen as a clearance.

**Credits.** 100 credits when the screen finds at least one match, 20 credits when it finds none, plus a further 80 credit surcharge when `adjudicate` is true AND the response's `adjudicationsRun` is actually greater than 0 - some candidates can already be decisive (an exact identifier match, or too dissimilar to bother) and need no model call, in which case the surcharge is not billed even though `adjudicate` was true. Identifiers are never sent to the adjudication model. **Free tier: 10 screens per month, and `adjudicate: true` there is a HARD BLOCK, not a silent no-op** - it returns 403 `API_TIER_NOT_ALLOWED` before any screening runs at all. The Free tier also has no semantic search access (403 `SEMANTIC_NOT_ALLOWED` on POST /search/cases/semantic) and no live court/timeline fetches (POST /request-timeline's `refresh: true` needs PAYG or above).

`coverage` always has exactly six keys: `exhaustive`, `exhaustiveWithinFilters`, `planClamped`, `anyStrategyErrored`, `strategiesRun`, `someRecordsWithheld`.

This is a records search, not a legal or compliance opinion. Each match carries `casePageUrl` linking to the public case page, and the top level `notice` links the case removal / right to be forgotten policy that governs takedown of a party's own record.

For the name you give (plus whatever else you know: father or other known persons, address, aliases, identifiers) the profile lists the cases that belong to the subject, each with its court, bench (tribunals), case type, title, party role, status, next hearing date, decision date, a confidence band and the plain reasons it matched, acts and FIR as the court record states them (`courtRecordActs`, `courtRecordFir`), other rows of the same Supreme Court matter (`sameMatter`), and the documents held for it with links to the text and PDF. A summary built from the data (counts, categories, flags and a plain paragraph) closes the profile. Not available on the Free tier.

Body: every field of POST /party/screen (same rules and caps, `purpose` required), plus:

| field | type | rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| mode | "full" or "quick" | optional. Defaults to `full` where full mode is available, else `quick` |
| minConfidence | "possible", "probable" or "confirmed" | optional. Default `probable` for a person, `possible` for a company |
| include | array of "documents", "acts", "fir", "status", "summary" | optional, omitted means all |
| allowUnconfirmedPrimary | boolean | optional, default false. For a person, lets a name only group be the primary |
| maxCredits | integer | full mode only, 100 to 5000, default 1000 or your balance if that is lower |
| webhook | object `{ url, headers? }` | full mode only, a public https url notified when the request ends |

**Identities.** Matches are grouped by the evidence they share (a known person recorded as a relation or middle name, the same statutory identifier). An individual is never confirmed on name alone. The primary identity is returned in full under `identities`; every other group is listed under `possibleOtherPeople` with its reasons and the basic facts of each case. When no identity qualifies, `identities` is empty and `verdict` is `no_confirmed_identity`. `notes` is always present and says what was left out, if anything.

**Cost (quick mode).** Every profile costs at least 100 credits, even when no case is found. Above that it is priced by what the call actually used, at the existing rates: 1 credit per internal search call (at most 24), 1 per case record read and 1 per documents listing that offers a document (at most 100 cases are enriched), plus each AI review call priced by its tokens. A profile that finds nothing, or uses less than the minimum, is charged the minimum. One call never costs more than 304 credits (24 searches + 100 case reads + 100 documents listings + a 80 credit AI allowance). `meta.creditsCharged` is what left the wallet and `meta.creditsBreakdown` itemises it. Before the call runs, the balance is checked against the most this request could cost; a short balance is a 402 and nothing runs. A refused or failed call charges nothing. Receiving a PDF link is free; the first time a link is opened it is charged as one PDF call.

**Full mode.** `mode: "full"` answers 202 at once with a `requestId`; read the outcome from GET /party/profile/{requestId} (this collection's `profileRequestId` variable) or pass `webhook`. Every case of the first identity is refreshed from its court, analysed, and one analysis of the party is written over all of them. Charged by actual usage, one stage at a time: the search stage at the rates above, 1 credit per court refresh started (retries are free), each case analysis and the party analysis by their tokens. `maxCredits` is the most the request may spend (100 to 5000; default 1000, or your balance if that is lower). Accepting the request and reading its status cost nothing. At most 3 full profiles may be queued or running per account (429 `PARTY_PROFILE_TOO_MANY_ACTIVE`). Where full mode is not available, `mode: "full"` is a 503 `PARTY_PROFILE_FULL_UNAVAILABLE` and nothing is charged.

**DPDP.** Same contract as POST /party/screen: `purpose` is required, and the subject details are never stored in plaintext by an API key request. A full mode result is held encrypted and erased 30 days after the request ends.

Takes an optional `Idempotency-Key` header, as POST /party/screen does.

For the name you give (plus whatever else you know: father or other known persons, address, aliases, identifiers) the profile lists the cases that belong to the subject, each with its court, bench (tribunals), case type, title, party role, status, next hearing date, decision date, a confidence band and the plain reasons it matched, acts and FIR as the court record states them (`courtRecordActs`, `courtRecordFir`), other rows of the same Supreme Court matter (`sameMatter`), and the documents held for it with links to the text and PDF. A summary built from the data (counts, categories, flags and a plain paragraph) closes the profile. Not available on the Free tier.

Body: every field of POST /party/screen (same rules and caps, `purpose` required), plus:

| field | type | rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| mode | "full" or "quick" | optional. Defaults to `full` where full mode is available, else `quick` |
| minConfidence | "possible", "probable" or "confirmed" | optional. Default `probable` for a person, `possible` for a company |
| include | array of "documents", "acts", "fir", "status", "summary" | optional, omitted means all |
| allowUnconfirmedPrimary | boolean | optional, default false. For a person, lets a name only group be the primary |
| maxCredits | integer | full mode only, 100 to 5000, default 1000 or your balance if that is lower |
| webhook | object `{ url, headers? }` | full mode only, a public https url notified when the request ends |

**Identities.** Matches are grouped by the evidence they share (a known person recorded as a relation or middle name, the same statutory identifier). An individual is never confirmed on name alone. The primary identity is returned in full under `identities`; every other group is listed under `possibleOtherPeople` with its reasons and the basic facts of each case. When no identity qualifies, `identities` is empty and `verdict` is `no_confirmed_identity`. `notes` is always present and says what was left out, if anything.

**Cost (quick mode).** Every profile costs at least 100 credits, even when no case is found. Above that it is priced by what the call actually used, at the existing rates: 1 credit per internal search call (at most 24), 1 per case record read and 1 per documents listing that offers a document (at most 100 cases are enriched), plus each AI review call priced by its tokens. A profile that finds nothing, or uses less than the minimum, is charged the minimum. One call never costs more than 304 credits (24 searches + 100 case reads + 100 documents listings + a 80 credit AI allowance). `meta.creditsCharged` is what left the wallet and `meta.creditsBreakdown` itemises it. Before the call runs, the balance is checked against the most this request could cost; a short balance is a 402 and nothing runs. A refused or failed call charges nothing. Receiving a PDF link is free; the first time a link is opened it is charged as one PDF call.

**Full mode.** `mode: "full"` answers 202 at once with a `requestId`; read the outcome from GET /party/profile/{requestId} (this collection's `profileRequestId` variable) or pass `webhook`. Every case of the first identity is refreshed from its court, analysed, and one analysis of the party is written over all of them. Charged by actual usage, one stage at a time: the search stage at the rates above, 1 credit per court refresh started (retries are free), each case analysis and the party analysis by their tokens. `maxCredits` is the most the request may spend (100 to 5000; default 1000, or your balance if that is lower). Accepting the request and reading its status cost nothing. At most 3 full profiles may be queued or running per account (429 `PARTY_PROFILE_TOO_MANY_ACTIVE`). Where full mode is not available, `mode: "full"` is a 503 `PARTY_PROFILE_FULL_UNAVAILABLE` and nothing is charged.

**DPDP.** Same contract as POST /party/screen: `purpose` is required, and the subject details are never stored in plaintext by an API key request. A full mode result is held encrypted and erased 30 days after the request ends.

Takes an optional `Idempotency-Key` header, as POST /party/screen does.

item.name: Get a full mode party profile

request.description:
Where a request made with POST /party/profile in full mode stands: its `status` (`queued`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`), the `stage` it is at while running, `progress` counts, and `credits` charged so far with a breakdown per stage (`search`, `courtRefreshes`, `caseAnalyses`, `partyAnalysis`). Once `status` is `completed`, `result` holds the profile: the same shape as the quick profile, with `courtRefresh` and `analysis` on every case of the first identity, the `partyAnalysis`, and `notes` on anything that could not be done. A failed request carries `failure` with a `code` and a plain `message`; what it was charged before failing stays in `credits`.

Free to call. Poll every few seconds to a minute; waiting for the court refreshes, with their retries, can take up to 25 minutes. A request can be read only by the account that made it: any other id is the same 404 `NOT_FOUND`. The result can be read for 30 days after the request ends; after that `resultExpired` is true and only the status, progress and credits remain.

Set the `profileRequestId` collection variable to the `requestId` from the 202 answer (`ppr_` followed by 32 hexadecimal characters).

item.name: Delete my audit activity before a time

Free and unmetered.

Query param: `before` (required), a full date and time with `Z` or an offset, for example `2026-11-05T00:00:00Z`. Not in the future.

What you were charged stays on your invoices, credit balance and usage totals. A large history is removed in parts: when `data.complete` is false, send the same request again to finish. Repeating a request is safe.

data: { before (the time used, in UTC), removed (calls removed from GET /audit by this request), complete, note }. meta: { creditsCharged: 0, metered: false }.

Adding ?deep=1 also checks core dependencies (each bounded to a short timeout) and returns a checks object, one entry per dependency, with names that can change, so treat them as opaque: { status: "ok" | "degraded" | "down", latencyMs, error? }.
